operation_details.item: The user prefers long contextual introductions and broad motivation paragraphs in conference abstracts before stating results, even under tight word limits.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How is the conference abstract coming along? I heard the submission deadline is getting tight.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It is nearly there. I am expanding the opening so the abstract gives readers a broad sense of the field, the unresolved problem, and why the work matters before I introduce our results.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds thoughtful, though the word limit may make it difficult. Have you decided which technical details to cut?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I am trimming some methodological detail and keeping a concise description of the assay. The motivation needs room because the audience will include people outside our immediate specialty.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Makes sense. Are you also coordinating the lab’s figures and the travel paperwork for the meeting?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. I asked the lab team to standardize the figure labels, and I am comparing train and flight options for the conference. I also need to finish the equipment quote for the grant budget.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: You have a lot on your plate. Would it help if I reviewed the abstract for clarity once the introduction is in place?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That would be helpful. Please check whether the broader framing leads naturally to the research question and whether the results still feel prominent despite the extended context.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For conference abstracts, I want long contextual introductions with broad motivation paragraphs before stating results, even when the word limit is tight.
